say: Each like runs three steps: read the count, add one, write it back.

say: Two likes arrive together. Both read nine hundred. Both add one. Both write nine hundred and one.

say: Two likes, but the count only went up by one. That's a race condition: two requests overlap, and one overwrites the other.
show: Two likes, but the count only went up by [one.] That's a *race condition:* two requests overlap, and [one overwrites the other.]

say: It hides in testing, because one person tapping never overlaps. It shows up under real traffic.

say: Like two people updating a tally on a whiteboard at the same time: whoever writes last erases the other's work.
show: Like two people updating a tally on a *whiteboard* at the same time: [whoever writes last] erases the other's work.

say: The fix: make read, add and write one step that can't be split.
show: The fix: make read, add and write *one step* that [can't be split.]

say: Engineers call this an atomic update. In SQL, set likes equals likes plus one, in a single statement. In Redis, the increment command does the same.
